L01.text: If the Sun vanished right now, you wouldn't even notice for eight minutes and twenty seconds.

L02.text: That's how long sunlight takes to reach us. And gravity travels at exactly the same speed.

L03.text: So for eight minutes, Earth keeps happily circling a Sun that isn't there.

L04.text: Then, lights out. Even the Moon goes dark. It was only ever a mirror.

L05.text: With nothing to orbit, Earth flies off in a straight line, at thirty kilometers every second.

L05b.text: The Moon tags along for the ride, still orbiting us, in the dark.

L06.text: Luckily, you won't freeze instantly. Unluckily, the first days each get about twenty degrees colder.

L07.text: Within a week, the whole planet is below freezing.

L08.text: The oceans freeze on top, but that ice works like a blanket. Underneath, the water stays liquid for thousands of years.

L09.text: And down by the volcanic vents, tube worms and shrimp that never needed sunlight just carry on.

L10.text: So the real survivors of the apocalypse? The shrimp.
